vulnerabilities.description: CVE-2022-0839 is an XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability in Liquibase Core versions prior to 4.8.0 via the SAXParser. An attacker could exploit this to read arbitrary files or perform server-side request forgery (SSRF) through crafted XML changelog files.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure 4.8.0+ includes the fix. All current Liquibase Secure distributions are built from source with the patched SAXParser configuration.
vulnerabilities.workaround: If using Liquibase < 4.8.0, disable XML changelog parsing or upgrade to 4.8.0+. Alternatively, ensure all changelog files come from trusted sources only.

ratings.justification: Code path containing the vulnerability is not present in Liquibase Secure builds. NVD score reflects theoretical maximum; contextual score reflects actual exploitability.

analysis.detail: XXE vulnerability fixed in Liquibase 4.8.0. Our liquibase-core is built from source with the fix included. Scanner incorrectly matches the non-semantic version format (master-<sha>).
False CPE match. liquibase-commercial-mongodb is a Liquibase extension, not MongoDB server. The vulnerability applies to MongoDB server only.

GraalVM Python setuptools path traversal vulnerability. setuptools is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its package management functions are never invoked at runtime. This CVE requires setuptools to process package inputs; no package installation or processing occurs at runtime.

vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run a Netty server.

ratings.justification: Server-side vulnerability. Liquibase never accepts inbound connections; Netty is only used as a client transport.

analysis.detail: Netty codec vulnerability fixed in 4.1.133.Final. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run any network server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections. There is no inbound socket for an attacker to exploit.

vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run a Netty server.

ratings.justification: Server-side transport vulnerability. Liquibase never accepts inbound connections; Netty is only used as a client transport.

analysis.detail: Netty epoll native transport vulnerability fixed in 4.2.13.Final. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run any network server. netty-transport-native-epoll provides the Linux epoll(7) native transport for outbound client connections. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport. There is no inbound socket for an attacker to exploit.

urllib3 vulnerability. urllib3 is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its HTTP client functionality is never invoked at runtime. All Python packages are pre-installed at build time via Maven graalpy-maven-plugin; no HTTP requests are made via Python at runtime.

vulnerabilities.description:
Improper Authorization vulnerability when multiple method constraints define an HTTP method for the same extension in Apache Tomcat.
This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.22, 10.1.55 or 9.0.118 which fix the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22, which includes the fix for the Tomcat 11.x affected range.

analysis.detail: Apache Tomcat improper authorization vulnerability fixed in 11.0.22. Liquibase Secure pins tomcat-embed-core through tomcat.version 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26), and the dependency uses that property (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:52). The fixed version is therefore present and the vulnerable 11.0.21 code is not.

vulnerabilities.description: An excluded subdomain constraint in a certificate chain does not restrict the usage of wildcard SANs in the leaf certificate. For example a constraint that excludes the subdomain test.example.com does not prevent a leaf certificate from claiming the SAN *.example.com.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 built with fixed Go 1.25.10.

ratings.justification: The lpm binary installed by the current Dockerfile is built from a Go toolchain version that includes the crypto/x509 fix.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib crypto/x509 name constraints vulnerability fixed in Go 1.24.11 and 1.25.5. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 declares go 1.25.10 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix.

vulnerabilities.description: CVE-2026-27142 fixed a vulnerability in which URLs were not correctly escaped inside of a <meta> tag's <content> attribute. If the URL content were to insert ASCII whitespaces around the '=' rune inside of the <content> attribute, the escaper would fail to similarly escape it, leading to XSS.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 built with fixed Go 1.25.10, and lpm does not use html/template.

ratings.justification: The html/template code path is not used by lpm, and the currently installed lpm release is built with the fixed Go toolchain.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib html/template escaping vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 declares go 1.25.10 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix. Defense in depth: lpm source contains no html/template usage, and the Liquibase Secure Docker entrypoint only calls lpm for optional driver installation when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4).

vulnerabilities.description: ReverseProxy can forward queries containing parameters not visible to Rewrite functions. When used with a Rewrite function, or a Director function which parses query parameters, ReverseProxy sanitizes the forwarded request to remove query parameters which are not parsed by url.ParseQuery. ReverseProxy does not take ParseQuery's limit on the total number of query parameters (controlled by GODEBUG=urlmaxqueryparams=N) into account. This can permit ReverseProxy to forward a request containing a query parameter that is not visible to the Rewrite function. For example, the query "a1=x&a2=x&...&a10000=x&hidden=y" can forward the parameter "hidden=y" while hiding it from the proxy's Rewrite function.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 built with fixed Go 1.25.10, and lpm does not use ReverseProxy.

ratings.justification: The net/http/httputil ReverseProxy code path is not used by lpm, and the currently installed lpm release is built with the fixed Go toolchain.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib net/http/httputil ReverseProxy query sanitization vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 declares go 1.25.10 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix. Defense in depth: lpm source contains no ReverseProxy or net/http/httputil usage, and the Liquibase Secure Docker entrypoint only calls lpm for optional driver installation when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4).

vulnerabilities.description: If a trusted template author were to write a <script> tag containing an empty 'type' attribute or a 'type' attribute with an ASCII whitespace, the execution of the template would incorrectly escape any data passed into the <script> block.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 built with fixed Go 1.25.10, and lpm does not use html/template.

ratings.justification: The html/template code path is not used by lpm, and the currently installed lpm release is built with the fixed Go toolchain.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty HttpObjectDecoder incorrectly terminates chunk header parsing at \r\n inside quoted strings in chunked transfer encoding extensions, enabling HTTP request smuggling.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run an HTTP server.

ratings.justification: Server-side HTTP vulnerability. Liquibase never accepts inbound HTTP connections; Netty is only used as a client transport.

analysis.detail: HTTP request smuggling via chunked transfer encoding in Netty HTTP codec. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious HTTP/1.1 requests to a Netty HTTP server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections. There is no listening socket for an attacker to exploit.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty verifyContinuationFrame fails to limit the number of zero-byte CONTINUATION frames, bypassing maxHeaderListSize and causing excessive CPU consumption on the server.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run an HTTP/2 server.

ratings.justification: Server-side HTTP/2 vulnerability. Liquibase never accepts inbound HTTP/2 connections; Netty is only used as a client transport.

analysis.detail: HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frame flood DoS in Netty HTTP/2 codec. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frames to a Netty HTTP/2 server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP/2 server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport. There is no inbound HTTP/2 listener.

vulnerabilities.description: See CVE-2026-33870 entry on netty-codec-http. Mirrored here so scanners that flag netty-transport receive the same not_affected statement.

analysis.detail: Scanner over-match: the vulnerable code lives in netty-codec-http (see the sibling assessment above). OWASP Dependency-Check and similar CPE-based scanners propagate the CVE onto netty-transport via the broad cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty:* match. netty-transport ships no HTTP/1.1 chunked decoder, so even if it were exposed as a server (which Liquibase is not), the affected code path would not run from this artifact.

vulnerabilities.description: Jackson Core 3.x StreamReadConstraints.maxDocumentLength check can be bypassed in multiple code paths, weakening DoS protection for applications that rely on it.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not rely on maxDocumentLength for protection.

ratings.justification: Liquibase does not use StreamReadConstraints.maxDocumentLength and does not process untrusted JSON input.

analysis.detail: Document length constraint bypass in Jackson Core 3.x. The StreamReadConstraints.maxDocumentLength check can be bypassed in blocking parsers, async parsers, and DataInput path. jackson-core 3.x is a transitive dependency from Spring Boot 4.0.3 in liquibase-license-utility. Liquibase does not set maxDocumentLength (zero usages in codebase), does not process untrusted JSON input from external sources, and is a CLI tool — not a network-facing service. The constraint bypass only matters if relied upon for DoS protection, which Liquibase does not.

vulnerabilities.description: Apache Tomcat authentication bypass where OCSP validation soft-fails even when soft-fail is explicitly disabled, allowing revoked client certificates to authenticate.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not start a Tomcat server.

ratings.justification: Server-side TLS authentication vulnerability. Liquibase never starts a Tomcat server or binds an HTTPS connector. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency present in the distribution JAR but never initialized.

analysis.detail: Authentication bypass due to CLIENT_CERT soft fail misconfiguration in Tomcat's OCSP validation. Requires an active HTTPS connector configured with CLIENT_CERT authentication and an OCSP responder. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that uses picocli for command-line parsing and never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No connector, no authenticator, no OCSP — the code is inert.

HTTP request/response smuggling via invalid chunk extension in Tomcat HTTP/1.1 parser. Requires an active HTTP listener processing inbound requests. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; the HTTP parser is never invoked.
Fixed in msal4j 1.15.1. Liquibase Secure uses msal4j 1.23.1, which includes the fix.

TLS 1.3 cipher suite preference order not preserved in Tomcat's SSL connector configuration. Requires an active TLS connector performing cipher negotiation. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or binds a TLS connector. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; no TLS handshakes occur.

Information disclosure via padding oracle vulnerability in Tomcat EncryptInterceptor (clustering component). Requires Tomcat clustering with EncryptInterceptor enabled. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or initializes clustering. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; EncryptInterceptor is never instantiated.

Information disclosure via improper encoding in Tomcat JsonAccessLogValve. Requires an active HTTP connector with JsonAccessLogValve configured and non-default relaxedPathChars/relaxedQueryChars values. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; no access log valves are configured or initialized.

Information disclosure via sensitive data in Tomcat log files from the Kubernetes cloud membership provider (clustering). Requires Tomcat clustering with Kubernetes membership enabled. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or initializes clustering. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; Kubernetes cluster membership is never initialized.

Incomplete OCSP verification in Tomcat's FFM/OpenSSL TLS integration. Requires an active TLS listener with client certificate authentication and OCSP validation configured. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or binds any TLS connector. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; the TLS and OCSP subsystems are never initialized.

vulnerabilities.description: Apache Tomcat RCE via Default Servlet partial PUT — file fragments uploaded to predictable temp paths trigger deserialization of assembled content. Also enables reading security-sensitive files.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not start a Tomcat server.

ratings.justification: Server-side RCE requiring HTTP PUT to a running Tomcat servlet container. Liquibase never starts Tomcat or accepts HTTP requests.

analysis.detail: Remote code execution and information disclosure via Tomcat Default Servlet partial PUT support. Requires an HTTP PUT request to a running Tomcat servlet container with partial PUT enabled. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts the Tomcat HTTP server, never deploys any servlet, and never opens any network port. The Default Servlet, partial PUT handling, and file session persistence code paths are never activated.

Denial of service via excessive memory consumption in Tomcat multipart upload processing. Requires sending a crafted multipart/form-data HTTP POST to a running Tomcat instance. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server and never accepts HTTP requests. The multipart parsing code path is completely inactive.

Denial of service via HTTP/2 stream reset memory leak in Tomcat. Requires an HTTP/2 connection to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never enables HTTP/2, and accepts no inbound network connections.

Denial of service via integer overflow in Tomcat multipart upload file size limit validation. Requires sending a crafted multipart HTTP upload to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server and never processes inbound HTTP requests or multipart uploads.

Denial of service via uncontrolled resource consumption in Tomcat HTTP/2 stream management. Requires an HTTP/2 client connecting to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never enables HTTP/2, and never binds a network port.
False CPE match. cassandra-driver-kerberos is not the Authenticator 2FA app. The vulnerability applies to the Authenticator mobile application.

Path traversal and potential RCE via regression in Tomcat Rewrite Valve URL normalization. Requires an HTTP request to a running Tomcat server with the Rewrite Valve configured. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never configures the Rewrite Valve, and never accepts HTTP requests.

vulnerabilities.description: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117. Older, unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version [FIXED_VERSION], which fixes the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure unless the license utility is customized to enable Tomcat WebDAV handling. Upgrade tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 or later if WebDAV support is added.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable Tomcat WebDAV LOCK and PROPFIND handlers require WebDAV servlet/configuration that is not present in the license utility.

analysis.detail: Unbounded request body reads in Tomcat WebDAV LOCK and PROPFIND handling affect Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. The license utility pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.21 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26, tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:52) through spring-boot-starter-web (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:60) and starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20), but no WebDAV servlet, WebDAV mapping, or PROPFIND/LOCK handler is configured in tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main or its application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1).

vulnerabilities.description: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat: HTTP/2 request headers were not validated, which may have triggered unexpected application behavior. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, and 10.0.0-M1 through 10.0.27. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure unless the license utility is customized to enable Tomcat HTTP/2 support.

ratings.justification: HTTP/2 is not enabled in the license utility, and tomcat-embed-core is pinned at the fixed version 11.0.22. Apache rates this CVE as Low severity in the Tomcat 11 security advisory.

analysis.detail: HTTP/2 request header validation gap in Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires HTTP/2 connections to a running Tomcat server. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not enable HTTP/2 — application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) sets no server.http2.enabled property and declares no HTTP/2 connector, and the codebase contains no HTTP/2-specific Tomcat configuration. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26), so the fixed version is installed regardless.

vulnerabilities.description: Exposure of HTTP Authentication Header to unexpected hosts during WebSocket authentication in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.2 through 9.0.117, 8.5.24 through 8.5.100, and 7.0.83 through 7.0.109. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure unless the license utility is customized to act as a Tomcat WebSocket client or server.

ratings.justification: Tomcat WebSocket APIs are not used by the license utility, and tomcat-embed-core is pinned at the fixed version 11.0.22. Apache rates this CVE as Low severity in the Tomcat 11 security advisory.

analysis.detail: Exposure of HTTP authentication headers to unexpected hosts during WebSocket authentication in Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires a WebSocket client following an HTTP redirect during authentication. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not use the Tomcat WebSocket client or server APIs. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no WebSocket endpoint definitions, and the codebase contains no ClientEndpoint/ServerEndpoint annotations or other WebSocket-related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

vulnerabilities.description: Authentication Bypass Issues vulnerability in digest authentication in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, and 8.5.0 through 8.5.100. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure unless the license utility is customized to enable Tomcat digest authentication.

ratings.justification: Tomcat digest authentication is not configured in the license utility, and tomcat-embed-core is pinned at the fixed version 11.0.22. Apache rates this CVE as Moderate severity in the Tomcat 11 security advisory.

analysis.detail: Authentication bypass in Tomcat digest authentication, where any unknown user presenting the password "null" was authenticated. Affects Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires Tomcat to be configured to use DigestAuthenticator. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not configure any Tomcat realm or authenticator. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no realm/authenticator definitions, and the codebase contains no DigestAuthenticator or related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

vulnerabilities.description: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity in LockOutRealm in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, and 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure unless the license utility is customized to enable LockOutRealm or any other Tomcat realm.

ratings.justification: Tomcat realms (including LockOutRealm) are not configured in the license utility, and tomcat-embed-core is pinned at the fixed version 11.0.22. Apache rates this CVE as Low severity in the Tomcat 11 security advisory.

analysis.detail: LockOutRealm treats user names as case-sensitive, reducing its effectiveness against brute-force attacks. Affects Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires Tomcat to be configured to use LockOutRealm. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not configure any Tomcat realm. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no realm definitions, and the codebase contains no LockOutRealm or related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

vulnerabilities.description: Jackson Core 3.x maxNestingDepth constraint bypass in multiple parser implementations, enabling DoS via StackOverflowError from deeply nested JSON input.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not parse untrusted JSON input.

ratings.justification: Liquibase only parses operator-controlled JSON files and does not rely on StreamReadConstraints for protection.

analysis.detail: Nesting depth constraint bypass in Jackson Core 3.x UTF8DataInputJsonParser and ReaderBasedJsonParser. maxNestingDepth from StreamReadConstraints is not enforced, allowing a deeply nested JSON document to cause StackOverflowError. Liquibase is a CLI tool that only parses JSON from trusted, operator-controlled configuration files and changelog artifacts. It does not expose any JSON parsing endpoint to remote or untrusted input. As established in the prior assessment of GHSA-2m67-wjpj-xhg9, Liquibase does not rely on StreamReadConstraints as a security boundary.

Netty SslHandler resource exhaustion vulnerability via SSLEngine. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious SSL/TLS data to a Netty server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run a TLS server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections.

Netty HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frame validation bypass in codec. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious HTTP/2 frames to a Netty HTTP/2 server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP/2 server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport.

vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run a Netty server.

ratings.justification: Server-side vulnerability. Liquibase never accepts inbound connections; Netty is only used as a client transport.

Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections. There is no inbound socket for an attacker to exploit.

The installed JAR is 13.2.1.jre11 which contains the fix. Microsoft's non-standard Maven versioning uses a classifier suffix instead of a standard version bump.

PostgreSQL JDBC driver channel binding bypass. The vulnerability only triggers when the JDBC connection property channelBinding is explicitly set to "require" (default is "prefer"). Liquibase does not configure channelBinding=require in any default configuration. The vulnerable enforcement code path in ConnectionFactoryImpl.doAuthentication() is not reachable under Liquibase's default configuration.

vulnerabilities.description: pgjdbc is an open source postgresql JDBC Driver. From version 42.2.0 to before version 42.7.11, pgjdbc is vulnerable to a client-side denial of service during SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication. A malicious server can instruct the driver to perform SCRAM authentication with a very large iteration count.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for builds using the current source dependency set; pgjdbc is managed at the fixed 42.7.11 version.

analysis.detail: pgjdbc client-side SCRAM-SHA-256 denial-of-service is fixed in 42.7.11. The current source sets postgresql.version to 42.7.11 (pom.xml:55), and the distribution dependency uses that managed version (dist/pom.xml:117). The fixed version is therefore present in the current Liquibase Secure build source even though the scanner reported 42.7.9 for this image.

Spring Boot EndpointRequest.to() creates a security matcher for null/** instead of the actuator endpoint path when the endpoint is disabled. Requires a running Spring Boot web application with Spring Security and actuator endpoint configuration. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context, never runs an HTTP server, never exposes actuator endpoints, and never configures Spring Security.

Spring Framework annotation resolution bypass in generic type hierarchies affecting @EnableMethodSecurity. Requires a running Spring application with method-level security annotations on generic type hierarchies. Liquibase is a CLI tool that does not use Spring Security, does not enable @EnableMethodSecurity, and does not start a Spring application context. The spring-core artifact is a transitive dependency.

GraalVM Python setuptools ReDoS vulnerability. setuptools is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its package management functions are never invoked at runtime. This CVE requires setuptools to parse HTML during package lookup; no package lookups occur since all packages are pre-installed at build time via Maven graalpy-maven-plugin.

vulnerabilities.description: In certain circumstances, Spring Boot's default web security is ineffective allowing unauthorized access to all endpoints. For an application to be vulnerable, it must be a servlet-based web application, have no Spring Security configuration of its own and rely on the default web security filter chain, depend on spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure, and not depend on spring-boot-health.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not include the actuator autoconfigure dependency required by this vulnerability.

analysis.detail: Spring Boot default web security bypass requires the application to depend on spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure and not depend on spring-boot-health. The repository's Spring Boot declarations are spring-boot-autoconfigure provided for Pro integration (pro/pom.xml:78) and spring-boot-starter-web in the license utility (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:44); grep for spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure, spring-boot-starter-actuator, and spring-boot-health across pom.xml files returned no matches.

vulnerabilities.description: A local attacker on the same host as the application may be able to take control of the directory used by ApplicationTemp. When server.servlet.session.persistent is set to true and the attack persists across application restarts, this may allow the attacker to read session information and hijack authenticated users or deploy a gadget chain and execute code as the application's user.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not configure persistent servlet sessions required to trigger this vulnerability.

analysis.detail: Spring Boot ApplicationTemp exploitation requires server.servlet.session.persistent=true and persistence across application restarts. Liquibase Secure's Docker image starts the Liquibase CLI entrypoint (docker/Dockerfile:68), and grep for server.servlet.session.persistent, ApplicationTemp, persistent=true, and setPersistent across Java, XML, properties, YAML, and YML files returned no matches.

Stack exhaustion DoS in json-smart via deeply nested JSON with many { characters (incomplete fix for CVE-2023-1370). Requires parsing attacker-controlled untrusted JSON input. Liquibase is a CLI tool that only processes JSON from local operator-controlled configuration files and database metadata. No network-facing JSON parsing surface exists.

Stack exhaustion DoS in json-smart via unlimited recursive parsing of deeply nested JSON arrays and objects. Requires parsing attacker-controlled untrusted JSON input. Liquibase is a CLI tool that only processes JSON from local operator-controlled configuration files and database metadata. No network-facing JSON parsing surface exists.

vulnerabilities.description: pgjdbc is an open source postgresql JDBC Driver. From version 42.2.0 to before version 42.7.11, pgjdbc is vulnerable to a client-side denial of service during SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication. A malicious server can instruct the driver to perform SCRAM authentication with a very large iteration count. With a large enough value, the client spends an unbounded amount of CPU time inside PBKDF2 before authentication can fail. A single attempt ties up a CPU core. Repeated or concurrent attempts exhaust client CPU and can wedge connection pools. In affected versions, loginTimeout did not fully mitigate this problem. When loginTimeout expired, the caller could stop waiting, but the worker thread performing the connection attempt could continue running and burning CPU inside the SCRAM PBKDF2 computation. This issue has been patched in version 42.7.11.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure distribution builds use PostgreSQL JDBC driver 42.7.11, which includes the fix.

analysis.detail: PostgreSQL JDBC SCRAM-SHA-256 client-side denial of service fixed in 42.7.11. Liquibase Secure distribution declares postgresql.version as 42.7.11 (dist/pom.xml:23) and uses that property for the org.postgresql:postgresql dependency (dist/pom.xml:115, dist/pom.xml:117), so the vulnerable 42.7.9 code reported by the scanner is not present in the current distribution build.

vulnerabilities.description:
Covert timing channel vulnerability in Legion of the Bouncy Castle Inc. BC-JAVA core on all (core modules). This vulnerability is associated with program files FrodoEngine.Java.
This issue affects BC-JAVA: from 1.71 before 1.84.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not use the affected Bouncy Castle Frodo post-quantum cryptography APIs.

analysis.detail: Bouncy Castle BC-JAVA FrodoEngine covert timing channel affects versions 1.71 before 1.84. Liquibase Secure distribution includes org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.78.1 (core/liquibase-dist/src/main/archive/licenses/commercial/README.txt:1318), but grep for FrodoEngine, Frodo, org.bouncycastle.pqc, pqc.crypto.frodo, and BCPQC across Java sources returned no matches, so the vulnerable Frodo post-quantum cryptography code path is not reachable.

vulnerabilities.description: XML External Entity (XXE) via Unsanitized Dictionary Parsing in Apache OpenNLP DictionaryEntryPersistor. Versions before 2.5.9 and before 3.0.0-M3 initialize dictionary XML parsing without secure processing or DTD restrictions, allowing attacker-supplied dictionary files to trigger local file disclosure or server-side request forgery during SAX parsing.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure. The vulnerable OpenNLP dictionary parsing API is not reachable from production code.

analysis.detail: OpenNLP DictionaryEntryPersistor XXE vulnerability fixed in 2.5.9. Liquibase Secure declares opennlp-tools through opennlp.version 2.5.8 (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/pom.xml:76) in the phileas AI services dependency (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:18, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:19, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:20), but the vulnerable dictionary XML parsing API is not imported or called. The only production OpenNLP usage found is document categorization and tokenization (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/src/main/java/ai/philterd/phileas/service/ai/sentiment/OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java:22, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/src/main/java/ai/philterd/phileas/service/ai/sentiment/OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java:23, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/src/main/java/ai/philterd/phileas/service/ai/sentiment/OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java:24).

vulnerabilities.description: Apache OpenNLP ExtensionLoader is vulnerable to arbitrary class instantiation via attacker-controlled input passed to the extension loading mechanism, potentially allowing remote code execution.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure. The vulnerable OpenNLP ExtensionLoader API is not reachable from production code.

ratings.justification: Liquibase does not invoke the OpenNLP ExtensionLoader. Only pre-bundled document categorization and tokenization APIs are used.

analysis.detail: Apache OpenNLP ExtensionLoader arbitrary class instantiation vulnerability. The ExtensionLoader API is not imported or called anywhere in Liquibase Secure. The only production OpenNLP usage is document categorization and tokenization via DoccatModel, DocumentCategorizerME, and WhitespaceTokenizer in OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java; no extension loading or dynamic class instantiation occurs.

vulnerabilities.description: Apache OpenNLP AbstractModelReader allocates unbounded memory when reading model files, allowing a malicious or malformed model file to cause an out-of-memory denial of service.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure. OpenNLP models are pre-bundled trusted artifacts; no attacker-controlled model loading occurs.

ratings.justification: Liquibase does not load model files from untrusted sources. Pre-bundled trusted models are used; AbstractModelReader is not directly invoked by Liquibase code.

analysis.detail: Apache OpenNLP AbstractModelReader OOM denial-of-service vulnerability via unbounded memory allocation during model loading. Exploitation requires loading an attacker-controlled or malformed model file. Liquibase Secure bundles pre-packaged, trusted OpenNLP model files at build time; no model files are loaded from external or user-controlled sources at runtime. AbstractModelReader is not imported or called directly in Liquibase code.

vulnerabilities.description: The Dial and LookupPort functions panic on Windows when provided with an input containing a NUL (0).
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure Docker images. The vulnerable behavior requires a Windows runtime environment, while the assessed image is Linux-based.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires Windows, but the assessed Docker image uses a Linux base image.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib Dial and LookupPort panic vulnerability requires Windows when processing input containing a NUL byte. The assessed Liquibase Secure Docker image uses the Linux base image eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2), so the vulnerable Windows runtime environment is absent.

GraalVM Python setuptools command injection vulnerability. setuptools is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its package management functions are never invoked at runtime. This CVE requires setuptools to process URLs via download/install functions; those functions are never called at runtime.

vulnerabilities.description: When using LookupCNAME with the cgo DNS resolver, a very long CNAME response can trigger a double-free of C memory and a crash.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. lpm does not call LookupCNAME and the cgo DNS resolver is not active on Linux.

ratings.justification: lpm never calls LookupCNAME. Hostname resolution for HTTP downloads uses LookupIPAddr. The cgo DNS resolver is not the default on Linux.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib LookupCNAME double-free in the cgo DNS resolver when processing a very long CNAME response. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it downloads Liquibase extension driver JARs from GitHub release assets via HTTP. lpm never calls LookupCNAME — standard HTTP hostname resolution uses LookupIPAddr/LookupHost, not the CNAME-specific API. Additionally, the vulnerability requires the cgo DNS resolver, which is not the default on Linux; the pure-Go DNS resolver is active in the eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble container.

vulnerabilities.description: When processing HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames, transport will enter an infinite loop of writing CONTINUATION frames if it receives a SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. lpm only connects to trusted GitHub release servers.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires a server to send SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE=0. lpm only connects to trusted GitHub release CDN endpoints; no attacker-reachable server is in the execution path.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib HTTP/2 transport infinite loop when a server sends SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it makes HTTP/2 connections to GitHub release servers to download Liquibase extension driver JARs. Exploitation requires a server to send the malformed SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE=0 frame. lpm only connects to trusted GitHub release CDN endpoints (URLs and checksums fixed in docker/Dockerfile:35-55); no attacker- controlled server endpoint exists in lpm's execution path.

vulnerabilities.description: Well-crafted inputs reaching ParseAddress, ParseAddressList, and ParseDate were able to trigger excessive CPU exhaustion and memory allocations.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. lpm has no email parsing functionality.

ratings.justification: lpm performs no email parsing. The net/mail code path is completely unreachable from any lpm operation.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib net/mail CPU exhaustion via pathological inputs to ParseAddress, ParseAddressList, and ParseDate. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image. lpm is a package manager for Liquibase extension drivers and has no email processing functionality. The vulnerable net/mail parsing functions are not called by lpm at any point during package installation or management operations.

vulnerabilities.description: Pathological inputs could cause DoS through consumePhrase when parsing an email address according to RFC 5322.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. lpm has no email parsing functionality.

ratings.justification: lpm performs no email parsing. The net/mail consumePhrase code path is completely unreachable from any lpm operation.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib net/mail DoS via pathological email address inputs reaching the consumePhrase parser (RFC 5322 phrase parsing). lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image. lpm is a package manager for Liquibase extension drivers and has no email processing functionality. The vulnerable net/mail consumePhrase code path is not reachable from any lpm operation.

vulnerabilities.description: The Reader.ReadResponse function constructs a response string through repeated string concatenation of lines. When the number of lines in a response is large, this can cause excessive CPU consumption.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 built with fixed Go 1.25.10.

ratings.justification: The Docker image installs lpm v0.3.4, whose upstream go.mod declares fixed Go 1.25.10. The lpm source also has no direct ReadResponse, net/textproto, or net/http usage.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib Reader.ReadResponse CPU exhaustion vulnerability fixed in Go 1.24.8 and 1.25.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), download it from the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 release (docker/Dockerfile:49), and the corresponding upstream liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3 declares go 1.25.10, which includes the fix. GitHub code search for liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 found no direct ReadResponse, net/textproto, or net/http usage, so the vulnerable API is not directly reachable from lpm source.

vulnerabilities.description: The ParseAddress function constructs domain-literal address components through repeated string concatenation. When parsing large domain-literal components, this can cause excessive CPU consumption.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 built with fixed Go 1.25.10 and lpm has no email parsing functionality.

ratings.justification: The Docker image installs lpm v0.3.4, whose upstream go.mod declares fixed Go 1.25.10. The lpm source also has no direct ParseAddress or net/mail usage.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib ParseAddress CPU exhaustion vulnerability fixed in Go 1.24.8 and 1.25.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), download it from the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 release (docker/Dockerfile:49), and the corresponding upstream liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3 declares go 1.25.10, which includes the fix. GitHub code search for liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 found no direct ParseAddress or net/mail usage, so the vulnerable email parsing API is not reachable from lpm source.
